nasa_numbers.quote: Twenty-four concurrent-flow tests were performed, focusing on finding flammability limits as a function of oxygen and flow speed.
nasa_numbers.statement: Number of concurrent rod tests analysed: 24.

nasa_numbers.quote: For blowoff limit tests, the astronaut quickly turned up the flow to obtain extinction.
nasa_numbers.statement: Blowoff protocol: flow turned up quickly until extinction.

nasa_numbers.quote: For quenching tests, the flow was incrementally turned down and the flame allowed to stabilize at the new flow condition for at least the solid-phase response time before changing it again.
nasa_numbers.statement: Quench protocol: flow stepped down with stabilization at each step (repeated on p.4 and p.9).

nasa_numbers.quote: Twenty-two rods were clear, and two were black, but no obvious differences between clear and black have been noted to date.
nasa_numbers.statement: Of the 24 tests, 22 clear rods and 2 black rods.

nasa_numbers.quote: Seventeen clear cast PMMA cylindrical rods of various diameters (11with 1/4”, 4 with 3/8”, and 2 with 1/2” diameters) were burned in a concurrent flow direction.
nasa_numbers.statement: 17 clear rod samples (counts per diameter); samples, not tests (some samples were reburned).

nasa_numbers.quote: The air velocity transducer probe had a response time of approximately one minute.
nasa_numbers.statement: Flow sensor response time ~1 min; p.2-3 continue: 'The fan voltage was calibrated with the air velocity transducer reading at the end of every operations day using that day's flow restrictor configuration(s).'

nasa_numbers.quote: Oxygen concentrations in the MSG working volume were varied during the testing from ambient ISS oxygen levels (~ 21% O2) down to ~14% O2
nasa_numbers.statement: Oxygen range of the tests: ~21% down to ~14% O2 (repeated in Conclusions, p.9).

nasa_numbers.quote: Quench test burns lasted up to 28 minutes.
The flow at blowoff was defined by the fan voltage reading at the moment the stagnation region opened up and the flame moved downstream.
nasa_numbers.statement: Blowoff flow comes from the fan voltage reading (via calibration), not from the Air display.

nasa_numbers.quote: the flame is unable to propagate upstream for the low oxygen levels tested (16.1% O2 and lower).
nasa_numbers.statement: Stagnation region could not be re-established after blowoff at 16.1% O2 and below.

nasa_numbers.quote: For each test, the flow at which the flames extinguished and the last flow where a stable flame was observed (or where the flame did not blowout in the drop time for drop tests), along with the post-burn oxygen reading were used to generate the flammability boundary, shown in Figure 4.
nasa_numbers.statement: Boundary points = extinction flow and last stable flow per test, with post-burn (final) O2.

Figure 4 legend text, read from the figure image (DERIVED_FROM_FIGURE): quench-branch fit; legend also reads 'Blowoff: 0.02x+13.3' and, for the drop-tower linear fit, 'y = 0.0181x + 13.42'. x axis 'Forced Stretch Rate, s-1', y axis 'Final O2 Concentration, % by volume'.

nasa_numbers.quote: Using the y-intercept of the linear fit (13.3 % O2 in the Figure 4 fit, versus the minimum test point of 13.6 % O2) would add a slight level of conservatism.
nasa_numbers.statement: Blowoff-branch y-intercept 13.3% O2; minimum test point 13.6% O2.

nasa_numbers.quote: The flow-induced stretch around the approximately spherical rod tip is af = 3/2 U/R.
nasa_numbers.statement: Forced stretch formula used for the Figure 4 x axis (R = rod radius, U = flow speed).

nasa_numbers.quote: Figure 4 currently shows the flammability boundary data plotted as forced stretch rate
nasa_numbers.statement: Figure 4 uses forced stretch only; curvature-induced stretch not yet included.
Rod radii (Figure 2 caption): R is radius, half of the 1/4, 3/8, 1/2 inch diameters.

limits: 1) No row yields an unambiguous Air display cm/s value for the last stable flow or the extinction flow: in every quench/blowoff row the limit is given as a pot setting or fan-display value (Fan display column), or as 'down to ext' with no number. NTRS p.5 states blowoff flow was taken from the fan voltage reading, and the Summary Report (PDF p.74) says a daily fan calibration associated fan voltage with flow; those calibration curves were not read here, so the cm/s values behind NASA's Figure 4 cannot be reproduced from these rows. 2) 29 rows are 'unclear' because the PSI cells show stepped, raised or alternating flows without an extinction/blowoff marker; for most of them the Summary Report Appendix A observation column (not in the PSI CSV) does state the outcome; those quotes are in 'note' but were not used, per the task rule. 3) Several Air display cells mix two series (O5a, O13a, O13b: parenthetical or main series in the fan-display range) and were not reconciled. 4) O20-O22 (2016, restrictor 0) are not in the Summary Report Table A.5 and postdate the NTRS paper; the 24 pre-2016 Olson rows (O1-O19 with a/b) match the paper's count of 24 tests and its 22 clear + 2 black split (black: O11, O14), but no mapping of individual rows to Figure 4 points was attempted. 5) Anomalies left as found: P17 fan display 233 > stated max 122; P22a final O2 0.6 and P22b final O2 39.1; decimals (38.5, 26.5, 2.5, 0.5) in Air display despite the units-only display; derived_radius_mm empty for P3b, P14, P15, P21a. 6) PDF page rendering was unavailable (pdftoppm missing); the NTRS PDF was read through its text layer plus the page images returned by the reader; Figure 4 legend values come from the figure image and carry DERIVED_FROM_FIGURE.
